patches.new_disclaimer: Includes BLM, USFS, NPS, FWS, and DoD holdings; expressed as a percent of the state's total land area. Includes Washington DC.
Total retail sales divided by resident population; low-population, tourism-heavy states punch above their weight. Includes Washington DC.
Counts land borders only; states separated only by water are not counted as neighbors. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Ranked by depth below sea level; rank 1 is the deepest below sea level. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Eight US states have a Great Lakes shoreline; the pool is exactly 8. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Includes volcanoes classified by USGS as historically active or potentially active. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Includes the Great Basin, Mojave, Sonoran, and Chihuahuan deserts. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Includes all classes of wetlands per NWI: freshwater, estuarine, and marine. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Counts documented caves per NSS state surveys; includes both wild and show caves. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Ranked by the longest single surveyed cave system located in each state. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Mean elevation is measured across the entire state land area, so terrain distribution matters more than the highest peak alone. Includes Washington DC.
Ranked by area of each state that drains to the Mississippi River (not total state area). DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Statewide averages from NOAA 1991-2020 normals. Individual sites (e.g. Mount Waialeale) far exceed statewide means. Includes Washington DC.
Rank 1 is the driest state (lowest inches per year). Statewide averages, not local extremes. Includes Washington DC.
Based on NWS annual counts for 1991-2020. Includes all confirmed tornadoes regardless of EF rating. Includes Washington DC.
Counts direct hurricane landfalls on each state's coast, per NOAA HURDAT2. A single storm crossing multiple states is counted once per state. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
Highest all-time official temperature per NOAA's State Climate Extremes Committee. Death Valley's 134°F (1913) remains debated but is the accepted official record. Includes Washington DC.
Rank 1 is the coldest ever recorded (most negative Fahrenheit). All-time official state minima per NOAA SCEC. Includes Washington DC.
Statewide averages derived from NOAA/NWS first-order station normals. Some states are averaged across multiple reporting stations. Includes Washington DC.
Rank 1 is the cloudiest state. Based on mean number of overcast days per NOAA/NWS station normals. Includes Washington DC.
